foraging.note: Authored seasonal gameplay estimates, not measured harvests or dietary vitamin C doses. Greens and berries supplement meals; four physical pounds supply one food unit. A shared half-pound of produce per living traveler counts as a vitamin-C meal.

produce_trade.note: Authored produce baskets, prices, drying and vitamin retention; not measured 1848 tariffs or nutrient assays. One basket represents four pounds of fresh produce, one food unit.

replacement_wagon.note: Empty covered wagon, no team or new household outfit. Period-informed $75 base estimate; regional prices apply. Post availability is an authored rescue opportunity, not a verified inventory.

wagon_guards.note: Authored offscreen camp abstraction. Guards use cached food, clothing and ammunition; one uncertain hunting shot per outing. Regional animals and health-based hauling apply. Protection lowers but never eliminates cache loss; outcomes are learned on return.

mounts.note: Authored load model, not measured 1848 animal specifications or safe handling guidance. Working total includes rider and fitted tack. Secured freight can be lashed outside saddlebags. Strenuous ceilings are emergency gameplay limits: actual excess load slows travel and increases wear; doubling is especially costly. Leading removes rider weight. Proper pack saddles avoid the improvised saddle-load wear surcharge.

shortfall.note: Authored gradual shortage model, not a clinical survival clock. Fractional missed ration-days accumulate; regular meals repay the deficit before health can recover. Hunger raises fatigue and later damage. Injury, exposure, illness and thirst remain separate.

food_energy.note: Calorie anchor for abstract food units, not a claim that every physical pound has equal energy. Existing purchased provisions remain an abstract mixed bundle at their existing weight/price. Generic lean meat uses a conservative rounded estimate; named game uses species values. Whole-unit rounding is a gameplay approximation.

pelts.note: Authored rough air-dried trade skins, not fully tanned buffalo robes. Recovery and scraping/drying cost one additional camp day and meals per batch; raw weights, one-day batch limit and prices are estimates. Historical robe prices are context, not direct prices for these goods.
